title: My Child Won't Eat! The Tale of the Stubborn Plate
summary:
The story repeats every day: "I don't like this!" your little one shouts, pushing the plate away. Sometimes they refuse vegetables, other times they abstain from meat, and sometimes they insist on eating only pasta. You feel frustrated and worried, wondering if they're getting enough, if they're growing healthily. The dining table turns into a battlefield, and you wonder when this difficult phase will end.

Know that picky eating is very common at this age and is often just a temporary and natural stage of development. Your child is exploring their independence and wants to have a say even in what goes into their body. Pressure and coercion will not work; in fact, they might make things worse and turn mealtime into a negative experience associated with stress instead of enjoyment and nourishment. Our goal is to build a healthy relationship with food, not a daily battle.

To calm the atmosphere, offer your child healthy and varied options, and let them choose the quantity that suits them. Be a role model by eating healthy and balanced meals yourself, and reduce sugary and unhealthy snacks between main meals. If you notice weight loss or a persistent refusal of entire food categories (such as all vegetables or all protein sources), do not hesitate to consult a pediatrician for reassurance or necessary guidance.
try_this: Tonight: Offer a plate with one new item alongside two items your child likes, without any comment or pressure to eat it.
